KM Saifuddin Ahamed, Advocate instructed by Mahmuda Begum, Advocate-on-Record—For the Respondents.

full_judgment:
Md Abdul Wahhab Miah J: This petition for leave to appeal has been filed by the Durnity Daman Commission (the Commission) against the judgment and order dated the 14th day of March, 2013 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 11155 .of 2008 making the Rule absolute. 

 2. Facts leading to the filing of this petition are that respondent No. 1 as petitioner (hereinafter referred to as the accused) filed an application before the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure (the Code) for quashing the proceedings of Special Case No. 1 (ka) of 2008 of the Court of Divisional Special Judge, Rajshahi Division, Rajshahi. The said special case arose out of a First Information Report (FIR) lodged by Dr Md Zahirul Islam, Deputy Civil Surgeon, Rajshahi on 29-5-2007 with Tanore Police Station implicating the accused along with 3(three) others alleging, inter alia, that as a part of operation "Alor Sondhaney," the Joint force found some medicine; some of those are expired, from outside the store room and, from the kitchen of storekeeper, Azizul Haque: in presence of the Civil Surgeon, Rajshahi, Upazila Nirbahi Officer (in charge), Rajshahi and the Officer-in-Charge, Tanore Police Station. The recovered articles were stored for misappropriation. On the basis of the said FIR, Tanore Police Station Case No.12 dated 29-5-2007 under sections 409/411/34 of the Penal Code was started: against the accused and 3(three) Others: The corresponding .GR number of the case is 66 of 2007. 

 3. Initially the investigation, of the case was taken up by the then, Officer-in-Charge of Tanore Police Station and then the case was investigated by the Commission and eventually, two charge-sheets were submitted on 6-3- 2008 being Nos. 30 and 30(ka) under sections 409/273/109 of the Penal Code and section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947: Eventually, the case was Sent to the Divisional Special Judge, Rajshahi where it was numbered as Special Case No. 1 of 2008. Then on the prayer of the Public Prosecutor, the cases were split up and another case being Special Case No. 1(ka) of 2008 was registered. Special Case No. 1 of 2008 was for the defalcation of money to the nine of Taka 7,43,977.15 for the period 17-8-2005 to 16-8-2006 and Special Case No.1(ka) of 2008 was for the defalcation of money to the tune of Taka 6,86,343.97 during the period 17-8-2006 to 29-5-2007. It further appears that charge was framed in the instant special case against the accused including the petitioner on 8-7-2008 under sections 409/273/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 to which the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. It further appears that prosecution Witness No.1 (PW 1) was examined on the 26th day of August, 2008 and thereafter as many as 17(seventeen) other witnesses, i.e. in total 18(eighteen) witnesses were examined out of 37(thirty seven) charge-sheet witnesses: The last witness was examined on 16-9-2008 and at that stage of the proceedings, the application for quashing the proceedings of the special case in question was filed. 

 6. The High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order made the Rule absolute mainly on the ground that no sanction was granted in respect to the submission of the charge-sheet. In the context, the High Court Division further observed that "sanction is a sine quo non for the reception of a charge-sheet, without which the Court concerned cannot take cognizance." The High Court Division further observed that "the language as figured in Rule 10 is such that investigation should be concluded in time." The High Court Division concluded that it was abundantly clear that "the mandatory provisions in section 32 had been ignored wherefore the proceeding must be taken to have been commenced as an abortive one." The High Court Division also observed that a Civil Surgeon should not be implicated for alleged theft committed at a store which remains under the control of a storekeeper, not under the direct control of a Civil Surgeon, in the view; this was an appropriate case where an initial inquiry should have been undertaken. 

 7. Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan, learned Advocate, appearing for the Commission, petitioner herein, has drawn our attention to the depositions of the witnesses examined in the case and has submitted that while examination of half of the prosecution witnesses was completed (total witnesses cited in the charge-sheet is 37), the accused-respondent filed the application before the High Court Division for quashing the impugned proceeding with main fide motive just to delay the disposal of the case. He has submitted that although, in the application filed under section 561A of the Code, the fact of examination of 18(eighteen) prosecution witnesses was not stated, by filing a supplementary affidavit the accused-petitioner annexed the certified copies of the depositions of the witnesses, but the High Court Division did not at all consider the said fact. He has further submitted that the High Court Division was wrong in holding that no sanction was granted by the Commission. Mr Khan has drawn our attention to the relevant portion of the charge-sheet to show that sanction was accorded by the Commission for submission of the charge-sheet. He has lastly submitted that the High Court Division exceeded its jurisdiction in making observation as to the merit of the case which, in fact, is the domain of the trial Court. 

 8. Mr KM Saifuddin Ahamed, learned Advocate, entering caveat on behalf of the accused-respondent, on the other hand, has supported the impugned judgment and order by submitting that although the prosecution in the meantime examined 18(eighteen) witnesses in the case, a perusal of the depositions would show that the petitioner had no complicity with the commission of the offence for which he was being tried and as such, the High Court Division rightly quashed the impugned proceedings. 

 10. Whether the accused had involvement with the occurrence as alleged by the prosecution or not is a question of fact and that has to be decided by the trial Court through sifting of evidence to be adduced by the prosecution. In the instant case, 18(eighteen) witnesses having already been examined, the trial Court should have been allowed to conclude the trial and dispose of the same in accordance with law. The High Court Division was not also correct in observing that "a Civil Surgeon should not be implicated for alleged theft committed at a store, which remains, under the control of a store keeper, not under the direct control of a Civil Surgeon, as such, observation is absolutely based on guess and surmises.
